newsitem.title: MEXICO: INTERVIEW - Mexico's Luismin sees gold output up.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Mexico's Luismin sees gold output up.

text.p: Industrias Luismin SA, the mining arm of Sanluis Corporacion, expects to decide in July on the building a pilot plant at its massive Metates gold project, director general Eduardo Luna said Thursday.
In an interview with Reuters, Luna said Luismin directors plan to meet their Metates joint venture partners Cambior Inc in Denver in two weeks.
"The final decision will be taken after that meeting, sometime in July," Luna said.
Metates in Durango state is classified by the 50-50 partners as a world class gold mine.
One study has proven and probable reserves at 10.5 million equivalent ounces of gold. Another estimate is a mineral inventory of 14 million ounces.
Luna said plans are for the pilot plant to be operated for at least 18 months to see how it functions through two rainy seasons.

He added the partners planned to mine gold and zinc at the deposit. "Zinc is an important economic element in the project," he added. But he said prospects looked bright for Metates despite ailing gold prices.
"There have been very good improvements in the laboratory tests...although right now gold prices do not help us," he said.

Luna added that prospects were improved given Luismin had hedged all expected gold output for next year at $413 per ounce and an average of $410 in 1999. "We believe that our cash flows are assured in this way" he added.

On the El Porvenir project in Aguascalientes state, Luna said Luismin and partners Hecla Mining Co expected a feasibility study to be finished in September. Afterward, the companies will define mine development plans, he said.

"On the question of El Porvenir, we expect it to enter into mine operations next year, but it is currently in the viability stage," he said, adding his estimate was that it could produce 50,000 to 70,000 equivalent gold ounces per year.
Luna said mine construction would be fast for El Porvenir because the project straddles a road and is only 30 minutes from the city of Aguascalientes.
The director general said Luismin planned to start test drilling the San Anton de las Minas project in Guanajuato state in the third week of July.

"We still do not know the size of this deposit. It could be anywhere between 500,000 to 1 million ounces. That could mean an (annual) output of between 50,000 to 100,000 ounces if what we believe is there is confirmed," he said.

Luna said the company's metals recycling plant in the city of Durango had started up and he anticipated an output of 30,000 equivalent ounces per year once it was fully underway. The plant is recycling computers, chips, switchboards and other electronic equipment to recover precious metals.

Luismin expected output this year to reach 165,000 equivalent ounces up from 152,000 ounces last year, Luna said, adding that to May, output goals were 21 percent ahead in gold and nine percent advanced in silver.
Weighted average costs to May totaled $194.99 per equivalent ounce of gold, he added.

Cost of production last year totaled $192 an ounce. He said increases in productivity and holding down costs had enabled Luismin to keep production costs at similar levels to last year in spite of inflation of about 27 percent.
Luismin's two mine ventures with Teck Corp were also in exploratory stages, Luna said.

At the El Oro project in State of Mexico he said nothing was yet defined but there had been good results and at the Tamara project in San Luis Potosi and Zacatecas states they were trying to define reserves.
((--Mexico City newsroom +525 7289530))
